To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

• IAC is a drive which makes the robot focus in situations which are neither predictable nor chaotic (i.e. neither too predictable nor unpredictable), and • IAC is the source of self-development: the robot autonomously shifts its attention from situations of low complexity to situations of higher complexity.
• Intelligent Adaptive Curiosity is a mechanism which enables an autonomous robot to develop by maximizing its learning progress.

• IAC is an adaptive mechanism which makes the robot focus its attention on situations in which it can maximize its learning progress, • IAC is a source of development for the robot because the situations in which it focuses its attention progressively increase in complexity over time, • IAC can be implemented with simple neural networks and is robust to the presence of noise in the environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the development of cognitive systems in the context of their interaction with the physical world.
the study of the emergence of intelligent adaptive curiosity in a robot which has to learn a complex, continuous and dynamic environment.
understanding the nature of curiosity and the mechanisms underlying the development of curiosity in infants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the IAC drive makes a robot autonomously and continuously develop in a process of progressive increase of the difficulty of the situations in which it is involved.
IAC is a drive which enables the robot to autonomously find situations in which its learning progress is maximal, and thus to autonomously develop.
the IAC system is a source of development: it makes the robot autonomously increase its activity complexity and its learning efficiency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is about the emergence of a self-organizing, autonomous and adaptive learning process in a robot.
we are developing a robot that is able to learn by interacting with its environment.
we have developed a system which enables the robot to autonomously increase its complexity of activity and its capabilities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IAC drive, which is an internal drive for the maintenance of the maximal learning progress, is a source of active development.
the IAC system is a mechanism which can autonomously build learning situations of increasing difficulty.

we have shown that the IAC system is a powerful source of selfdevelopment: the robot autonomously increases the complexity of its behavior, and thus its learning progress, by itself, without any external guidance or supervision.
